title: fix(plugin-approvals): an out-of-office delegation applies only in its own organization
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuGEYT5aVm7ttZRBJJNvF8Bj)_

Fixes #25280

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changed

`ApprovalService.lookupActiveDelegation` now reads a `sys_approval_delegation` row the way `grantAppliesInTenant` (`@objectstack/core`, `resolve-authz-context.ts`) reads a stored position or permission-set grant: the row reroutes an approver only when its `organization_id` is the request's organization, and both must name one.

| Delegation row | Request | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| org A | org A | reroutes | reroutes |
| org A | org B | no | no |
| no organization (`NULL`, absent, blank) | any | **reroutes in every organization** | no, and a `warn` names the row |
| any | no organization | **takes every active row** | no |

- `organizationNamed()` normalizes `NULL`, absent and `''` to "none", as core's module-private `grantOrganizationOf` does. It is applied to both sides of the comparison.
- An active organization-less row that the lookup skips is logged at `warn`. The structured fields are `{ delegationId, delegatorId, delegateId, requestOrganizationId }`, and the message gives the remedy. Its author still sees the row in Setup, and nothing else says it has stopped applying.
- The rule is the same in every posture (ADR-0131 D11). There is no posture branch.
- `sys_approval_delegation.organization_id` help, which said "null = applies across tenants for this delegator", now says what the code does:
  - `en` is regenerated with `node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write`.
  - `zh-CN`, `es-ES` and `ja-JP` are translated by hand. The `es-ES` and `ja-JP` leaves were byte copies of the old English, so their source-hash entries drop on extract.
- The object docblock and `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` (Out-of-office delegation) state the organization scope.

## Who is affected

**Under a wall (`group`/`isolated`), only stored state is affected.** No current write produces an organization-less delegation:
- A session insert is stamped with the active organization (`injectTenantOnInsert` in `sql-driver.ts`).
- An elevated insert with no organization is refused (`resolveSystemInsertOrganization`, D9).
- An update that empties the column is refused (`denyOrganizationRemoval`, `security-plugin-write-tenant-wall.ts`).

What remains are rows stored before 18.0. The D10 ceremony has no anchor for this table under a wall (inventory fate 3), so it reports such a row and leaves it `NULL`. Before this change, that row rerouted every organization's approvals for its delegator, onto a delegate who may hold no membership there.

**Under `single`, a delegation written on 18.x applies exactly as before.** D9 stamps the Default Organization on both the delegation and the record, and the request takes its record's organization. Only a pre-ceremony organization-less row stops applying, and `os migrate organization-ownership --apply` attributes it.

The changeset declares the break (`**BREAKING**`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker) and gives the operator remedy for each posture. Precedent: `.changeset/24583-7a2-organization-less-grant-readers-retired.md`.

## Tests

New file `ooo-delegation-organization.test.ts` (18 cases). Each walled case runs under both `isolated` and `group`:
- A's delegation does not reroute an approval in B, and the request lands in B.
- The same-organization delegation still applies, with the audit comment unchanged.
- The request's organization is its record's: a member signed in to A, opening on B's record, gets no reroute from A's delegation.
- An organization-less row reroutes nothing in either organization and is reported once per lookup, with the named fields.
- A blank or absent organization counts as organization-less.
- Beside an organization-less row, the same-organization row is the one that applies.
- A chain stops at an organization-less hop.
- A request with no organization takes no delegation.
- Under `single`, a Default-Organization delegation reroutes, and an organization-less row does not and is reported.

`approval-service.test.ts`: the pin "a null-org rule applies across tenants" is replaced by its inverse.

Fixtures that wrote an organization-less delegation and expected a reroute now write it in the request's organization:
- `admin-exemption-retired.test.ts`: `seedDelegation` writes `'t1'`.
- `admin-rescue-named-slate.integration.test.ts`: `dlg_admin` writes `ORG`, and `sys_approval_delegation` leaves the `relaxTenantColumns` list.
- `approval-notification-body.integration.test.ts`: `dlg_1` and `dlg_2` write `orgOfDeal(...)`, and `sys_approval_delegation` leaves the `relaxTenantColumns` list.

The three `installDefaultOrganization` suites that insert a delegation (`actor-lookups-hold-ids`, `approval-notification-keyed-text`, `approval-requested-notification`) pass unchanged. D9 stamps the Default Organization on both sides there.

`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` records the new test file's double (`check-engine-double-contract --write`). Its `update`/`delete` open with `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`/`assertEngineDeleteDispatch`, and its `find` holds the caller's `limit`.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run`: 95 files, 1232 tests, all passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck` passed, including `check:test-typecheck`.
- Ablation (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`): the old filter was restored in `approval-service.ts`, then the new file, `approval-service.test.ts` and the three re-stamped fixtures were run.
  - 10 tests went red: the organization-less, blank or absent, chain, no-organization-request and `single` organization-less cases, plus the replaced pin.
  - The cross-organization and same-organization cases stay green under the old filter, as expected: the old filter already kept a scoped row in its own organization.
  - After the restore, the file matched HEAD and `git diff HEAD` was empty.
- `node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs`: OK, all bundles in sync.
- `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main`: exit 0.
- Local gates (`dispatch-gates --commands`): on the first pass 95 of 99 exited 0. The other four were handled as follows:
  - `check:engine-double-contract` and `check:objectql-double-limit`: fixed (see above).
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:skill-examples`: exit 3 because their prerequisite dists were missing. Those packages are now built.
- The full re-run of the gates on the final head and the full dogfood battery (the `(narrowing)` arm) are running now. Their counts go in the `os-dev-report` on #25280.

## Acceptance notes

- The branch is the harness-assigned `claude/project-thread-4a6wrl`, not `claude/issue-25280-…`.
- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` gains one paragraph on the organization scope, so the guide states the behaviour this PR changes.
- #25342 (delegator prefill, in flight) edits the same object file and bundles, but only the `delegator_id` default and help. Whichever lands second merges main and regenerates the bundles.
- The remedy for a walled organization-less row is in the warning and the changeset: recreate the delegation while signed in to the right organization, then delete the old row. No automated rewrite is offered, because under a wall the row names nothing to attribute it by.
